---
title: "Validation"
---

`stokesjx` is benchmarked against the analytical solutions of Kramer, Davies and Wilson
(2021) and follows the propagator-matrix formulation of Hager and O'Connell (1981). For
each check, the bound of the test comes first and the measured agreement second.

## The error metric

The values are compared with the metric `e_l`: per degree, the largest difference over
the source nodes divided by the largest reference value.

## Analytical solutions

The benchmark is the set of analytical solutions of Kramer, Davies and Wilson (2021),
through the package `assess`. They cover an isoviscous shell, delta and smooth forcing,
free slip and no slip, with a uniform gravity and no self-gravitation. Bound `1e-12`,
measured 1.2e-14.

## The formulation in the literature

The kernels follow the propagator-matrix formulation of Hager and O'Connell (1981), with
the self-gravitation of Richards and Hager (1984) and Ricard, Fleitout and Froidevaux
(1984), the geoid kernels of Hager and Clayton (1989) and the compressible terms of
Forte and Peltier (1991). [The physics page](physics.qmd) derives each equation, and a
symbolic test (`tests/test_equations_symbolic.py`) derives the matrix of the radial
system again with sympy.

## The mpmath reference

A second solver computes the kernels at 50 to 250 digits with mpmath
(`tests/reference_mpmath.py`). It uses the single product of the propagators, the
algorithm that needs high precision, and not the sweeps of the package. It is
independent of the package in its algorithm and its arithmetic.

| Case | Bound | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| moderate cases, degrees 1 to 200 | `1e-12` | at most 8.5e-14 |
| stiff lid and ten decades of viscosity | `1e-11` | at most 1.2e-12 |
| 32 flag combinations | `1e-12` | at most 4.6e-13 |
| the viscosity cut | `1e-12` | at most 1e-13 |

## Derivatives

Every derivative passes the Taylor tests of [the derivatives
page](gradients.qmd#taylor-tests), with both signs and both modes, and every negative
control fails. The jvp/vjp dot products agree to `1e-12` (1e-14 typical).
